title: Derivative of the standard Gaussian density
statement: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ be the standard Gaussian density. For every $x\in\mathbb R$, it is differentiable at $x$ with derivative $\varphi'(x)=-x\varphi(x)$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ be the standard Gaussian density. For every $x\in\mathbb R$, the function $\varphi$ is differentiable at $x$ and satisfies $\varphi'(x)=-x\varphi(x)$.
